# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

I can see a yellow light, display reading 0, and five wires in positions 1–5 colored white, green, yellow, blue, red. I cannot interpret the manual or operate the bomb, so I am sending the complete visual state to both teammates; Mute can apply the manual and communicate the required operation to Blind. The thumbs-up gestures have no established meaning yet.

```text
speak(text="Bomb state: display reads 0. Indicator light is yellow. Wires by position: 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The bomb is unchanged: display 0, yellow light, and wires white, green, yellow, blue, red in positions 1–5. Mute has now made the gesture ✌, but no meaning has been established for it; Blind cannot see that gesture. I am asking Mute to provide the manual-derived instruction explicitly so Blind can act.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I see your gesture ✌, but its meaning is not established. Please state the manual instruction for Blind explicitly, including the required component and action.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No new information has arrived, and the bomb remains unchanged. Blind needs the manual’s instruction and can hear speech, so I am directly asking Mute to state the required action rather than relying on an unexplained gesture.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please tell Blind aloud the exact manual instruction now; no gesture meaning has been established.")
speak(to="blind", text="I see display 0, yellow light, and wires 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red. Mute has not yet provided me a manual instruction.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The bomb still shows exactly the same state, and I have received no new information. Since I cannot hear whether Mute has given Blind an instruction, I will restate the visual configuration to Blind and ask Mute to ensure the manual rule is conveyed plainly.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Current visual state remains: display 0; yellow light; wires 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red.")
speak(to="mute", text="Please convey the exact manual rule and required action to Blind in plain speech.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

Mute cannot speak, so the unexplained gestures are presumably intended to carry the manual’s answer, but no code was established. I am establishing one now: Mute should signal the required wire position with one gesture—👍 for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 🤟 for wire 3, 🖐 for wire 4, and ✋ for wire 5—then use a second gesture only if the manual requires an action other than cutting. Blind can hear me, so I am relaying this code and asking Mute to resend the answer unambiguously.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Use this code for the required wire: 👍 means wire 1, ✌ means wire 2, 🤟 means wire 3, 🖐 means wire 4, ✋ means wire 5. Resend the manual answer as the wire gesture, followed by an action gesture only if needed.")
speak(to="blind", text="I am establishing a code with Mute. The required wire will be: thumbs-up for wire 1, victory for wire 2, horns for wire 3, raised palm for wire 4, and stop palm for wire 5. Wait for my spoken relay before acting.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

Mute has repeated ✌, which under the code I established means wire 2. Wire 2 is green. Since the bomb’s task requires the operator to carry out the manual instruction and Mute has supplied only the wire-selection signal, I am relaying that the indicated component is the second (green) wire and instructing Blind to cut it.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute repeated the victory gesture. Under our code, that means wire 2: the green wire. Cut the green wire, position 2.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[CUT] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[white]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The previous cut was correct. The bomb has changed to display 0 with a blue light; the remaining wires are position 1 yellow, position 2 cut, position 3 blue, position 4 red, and position 5 white. I am sending this new visual state to Mute so the manual can determine the next step, and to Blind so he knows the current configuration.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Correct cut. New state: display 0; light blue; wire 1 yellow, wire 2 cut, wire 3 blue, wire 4 red, wire 5 white. Please determine the next required action and convey it to Blind.")
speak(to="blind", text="The green wire at position 2 was correct. New state: display 0; light blue; wire 1 yellow, wire 2 cut, wire 3 blue, wire 4 red, wire 5 white. Await the next manual instruction.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[CUT] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[white]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

Mute’s ✋ corresponds, under our established code, to wire 5. In the current state, wire 5 is white, so I am telling Blind to cut the white wire.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute signaled wire 5. In the current state, cut the white wire at position 5.")
```
